rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means a life characterized by constriction, as though it said a life possessing constriction.
rows.anchor: فكأنه قال : معيشة ذات ضنك

rows.speaker: جمع من المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes take the constricted life as worldly: believers who trust God live well, while unbelievers remain greedy, anxious, and sometimes humiliated; revelation links obedience with provision.
rows.anchor: فقال به جمع من المفسرين وذلك لأن المسلم لتوكله على الله يعيش في الدنيا عيشا طيبا

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود وأبو سعيد الخدري وعبد الله بن عباس
rows.claim: They identify the constricted life with punishment in the grave.
rows.anchor: فهذا قول عبد الله بن مسعود وأبي سعيد الخدري وعبد الله بن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra attributes to the Prophet a report that the unbeliever is punished in the grave by ninety-nine dragons.
rows.anchor: ورفعه أبو هريرة إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( إن عذاب القبر للكافر قال والذي نفسي بيده

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad al-Makhzumi and means the grave's pressure that displaces the ribs.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : نزلت الآية في الأسود بن عبد العزى المخزومي والمراد ضغطة القبر تختلف فيها أضلاعه

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والكلبي
rows.claim: Hasan, Qatada, and al-Kalbi understand it as constriction in Hell, where food and drink are agonizing and its inmates neither die nor live.
rows.anchor: فلا يموتون فيها / ولا يحيون وهذا قول الحسن وقتادة والكلبي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says it is spiritual constriction: the doors of good close before a person, who cannot find guidance to any good.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : المعيشة الضنك هي أن تضيق عليه أبواب الخير فلا يهتدي لشيء منها

rows.speaker: الشبلي
rows.claim: Al-Shibli explains that the truly afflicted are heedless of God; their punishment is to be left to themselves, an especially constricted condition.
rows.anchor: سئل الشبلي عن قوله عليه السلام : ( إذا رأيتم أهل البلاء فاسألوا الله العافية ) فقال أهل البلاء هم أهل الغفلات عن الله تعالى

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says the constricted life is that of an unbeliever, who lacks certainty about reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: وعن عطاء قال : المعيشة الضنك هي معيشة الكافر لأنه غير موقن بالثواب والعقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading compares this to 17:97, where people are gathered blind, mute, and deaf; a person may be sighted until being driven to the gathering, then blinded, as discussed at the passage on the blue-eyed.
rows.anchor: هذا مثل قوله : { ونحشرهم يوم القيامة على وجوههم عميا وبكما وصما }

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك ومقاتل
rows.claim: They say the person is blind to the proof; Sa'id ibn Jubayr transmits this interpretation from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد والضحاك ومقاتل : يعني أعمى عن الحجة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr reports Ibn Abbas's interpretation that the blindness is blindness to the proof.
rows.anchor: وهي رواية سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi calls the proof-blindness interpretation weak: people must recognize the falsity of their former beliefs in the afterlife, so they cannot literally be blind to the distinction between truth and falsehood; it also conflicts with their former sight.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : هذا القول ضعيف لأن في القيامة لا بد أن يعلمهم الله تعالى بطلان ما كانوا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the Qadi's objection rests on Mu'tazilite principles and sharply distinguishes his own account from that foundation.
rows.anchor: وبين هذه الطريقة وبين طريقة القاضي المبنية على أصول الاعتزال بون شديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that ignorant souls remain ignorant after leaving their bodies, and this ignorance becomes a source of the greatest spiritual pain in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن تحقيق الجواب عن هذا الاعتراض مأخوذ من أمر آخر وهو أن الأرواح الجاهلة في الدنيا

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i takes blindness to mean that the person finds no path to good on Judgment Day and stands bewildered like someone unable to see a way.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي : المراد من حشره أعمى أنه لا يهتدي يوم القيامة إلى طريق ينال منه خيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that God makes the rejecter blind as requital for abandoning and turning away from guidance.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى إنما أنزل به هذا العمى جزاء على تركه اتباع الهدى والإعراض عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, souls that leave their bodies ignorant and disconnected from spiritual beings retain that state, and their spiritual pain intensifies; their worldly rejection of evidence explains the blindness.
rows.anchor: هو أن الأرواح البشرية إذا فارقت أبدانها جاهلة ضالة عن الاتصال بالروحانيات بقيت على تلك الحالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who interpret constricted life as worldly take the passage to pair worldly hardship for turning from remembrance with blindness in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ومن فسر المعيشة الضنك بالضيق في الدنيا ، قال إنه تعالى

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes transgression to mean associating partners with God and unbelief.
rows.anchor: اختلفوا فيه فبعضهم قال : أشرك وكفر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes transgression to mean disobeying God.
rows.anchor: وبعضهم قال : أسرف في أن عصى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about not believing God's signs explains what is meant by transgression.
rows.anchor: لأن ذلك كالتفسير لقوله : أسرف وبين أنه يجزي من هذا حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife punishment is harsher because of its magnitude and more lasting because it never ends.
rows.anchor: أما الأشد فلعظمه ، وأما الأبقى فلأنه غير منقطع

none: Only Qur'anic text is present; the segment contains no commentary.

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says the verse establishes God's obligation to provide the enabling لطف that leads people to believe; otherwise they could ask why it was withheld or why no messenger was sent, and such an objection works only if they would believe upon obeying.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي : هذه الآية تدل على وجوب فعل اللطف إذ المراد أنه يجب أن يفعل بالمكلفين

rows.speaker: الكعبي
rows.claim: Al-Ka'bi says the hypothetical plea for a messenger proves God accepts arguments from servants; 21:23 means only that God acts justly, and inability to obey would give people their strongest argument.
rows.anchor: قال الكعبي قوله : { لولا أرسلت إلينا رسولا } أوضح دليل

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Razi's school infers that obligation and punishment arise only through revealed law; otherwise punishment would precede the law's arrival.
rows.anchor: قال أصحابنا : الآية تدل على أن الوجوب لا يتحقق إلا بالشرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each side, the believers and their opponents, awaits the outcome of its affair; this waiting may occur before death, at death, or after death when reward and punishment distinguish the vindicated from the false.
rows.anchor: أي كل منا ومنكم منتظر عاقبة أمره وهذا الانتظار يحتمل أن يكون قبل الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise that they will know who follows the straight path is a threat and rebuke to unbelievers, not an expression of doubt.
rows.anchor: وليس هو بمعنى الشك والترديد ، بل هو على سبيل التهديد والزجر للكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual feminine كانتا is used rather than a plural because the plural noun heavens denotes one genus, paired here with earth as a second genus.
rows.anchor: إنما قال كانتا رتقا ولم يقل كن رتقا لأن السموات لفظ الجمع والمراد به الواحد الدال على الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ratq means closure or joining, while fatq is the separation of two things that had been joined.
rows.anchor: الرتق في اللغة السد ، يقال : رتقت الشيء فارتتق والفتق الفصل بين الشيئين الملتصقين

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj analyzes ratq as a verbal noun, with the meaning that heaven and earth were two things possessing closure.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : الرتق مصدر والمعنى كانتا ذواتي رتق

rows.speaker: المفضل
rows.claim: Al-Mufaddal explains that the verse does not say “two ratqs” because each of the two is itself a ratq, as each individual is a body in 21:8.
rows.anchor: قال المفضل : إنما لم يقل كانتا رتقين كقوله : { وما جعلناهم جسدا لا يأكلون الطعام }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is called a roof because, in relation to the earth, it is like the roof over a house.
rows.anchor: سمى السماء سقفا لأنها للأرض كالسقف للبيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that the sky is protected from falling, as ordinary roofs may fall; cited verses say God holds it up and sustains the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: أن محفوظ من الوقوع والسقوط الذين يجري مثلهما على سائر السقوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is that the sky is protected from devils, as stated in 15:17.
rows.anchor: الثاني : محفوظا من الشياطين قال تعالى

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One account says angels protect the sky from devils.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه محفوظ بالملائكة من الشياطين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another account says stars protect the sky from devils.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أنه محفوظ بالنجوم من الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers protection by angels because it magnifies the gift of divine guardianship; stars are not needed to prevent harm to the sky from jinn stealing a hearing.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول أقوى لأن حمل الآيات عليه مما يزيد هذه النعمة عظما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky's signs are the evidences and lessons in its movements, directions, risings and settings, and the precise order of conjunctions and separations, all showing wisdom and power.
rows.anchor: معناه عما وضع الله تعالى فيها من الأدلة والعبر في حركاتها وكيفية حركاتها وجهات حركاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has the singular آيتها, understood generically: people notice worldly benefits from the sky but turn away from its manifest evidence for the Creator's existence and oneness.
rows.anchor: قرىء عن آيتها على التوحيد والمراد الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After saying people ignore the sky's signs, Razi details them: sun and moon complete God's favors by producing day and night and benefits through seasonal change and their orbital motions.
rows.anchor: لما قال : { وهم عن ءاياتها معرضون } فصل تلك الآيات ههنا

rows.speaker: جمهور الفلاسفة وأصحاب الهيئة
rows.claim: Most philosophers and astronomers posit a shared daily motion from east to west and a second, slower west-to-east motion, visible in the planets and inferred for the fixed stars from their changing positions.
rows.anchor: ثم قال جمهور الفلاسفة وأصحاب الهيئة ، وههنا حركة أخرى من المغرب إلى المشرق

rows.speaker: جمهور الفلاسفة وأصحاب الهيئة
rows.claim: Their evidence is that a faster planet passes a slower one eastward after conjunction; the moon's nightly apparent movement away from the sun illustrates this, and fixed stars likewise shift slowly along the zodiac.
rows.anchor: واستدلوا عليها بأنا وجدنا الكواكب السيارة كلما كان منها أسرع حركة إذا قارن ما هو أبطأ حركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects two simultaneous motions of one body in opposite directions: that would require it to be in two places at once; interruption of the spheres conflicts with philosophers' own premises.
rows.anchor: لزم كون الجرم الواحد متحركا حركتين إلى جهتين مختلفتين دفعة احدة وذلك محال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says the eastern motion might stop during western motion and resumes the millstone-and-ant example of opposite movements; Razi replies that uninterrupted spheres are required by the philosophers' own principles and that the analogy cannot overturn his proof.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل : لم لا يجوز أن يقال : الشمس حال حركتها إلى الجانب الشرقي تنقطع حركتها إلى الجانب الغربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the evidence for eastward motion is weak: all spheres may move eastward at different speeds, with slower spheres merely lagging, from the outermost and fastest down to the moon; this better fits cosmic order, with earth at rest.
rows.anchor: أما الذي احتجوا به على أن للكواكب حركة من المغرب إلى المشرق فهو ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bodies also move in latitude, north and south; without this inclination, effects would be confined to one place or produce permanent extreme seasons, while appropriately paced cycles spread benefit and avoid excess.
rows.anchor: أما حركاتها في عروضها فظاهرة وذلك بسبب اختلاف ميولها إلى الشمال والجنوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The measured duration of motion in each direction lets the celestial effects mature without excess or deficiency, while the intellect grasps only a little of creation's secrets.
rows.anchor: إذا كان هناك ميل يحفظ الحركة في جهة مدة ثم ينتقل إلى جهة أخرى بمقدار الحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural “they swim” includes stars along with the sun and moon, so the pronoun supplies the plural referent even though stars were not named earlier.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز أن يقول : { وكل فى فلك يسبحون } إلا ويدخل في الكلام مع الشمس والقمر النجوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, falak denotes anything circular, and its plural is aflak.
rows.anchor: الفلك في كلام العرب كل شيء دائر وجمعه أفلاك

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the falak is not a body but the orbit or track of the celestial bodies.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم : الفلك ليس بجسم وإنما هو مدار هذه النجوم وهو قول الضحاك

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most scholars say the falak is a physical body on which the stars move; Razi says this is closer to the Qur'an's apparent wording.
rows.anchor: وقال الأكثرون : بل هي أجسام تدور النجوم عليها ، وهذا أقرب إلى ظاهر القرآن

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One account describes the falak as a wave held together, in which the sun, moon, and stars run.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم : الفلك موج مكفوف تجري الشمس والقمر والنجوم فيه

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the falak is gathered water through which the planets swim, reasoning that swimming occurs only in water.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي : ماء مجموع تجري فيه الكواكب واحتج بأن السباحة لا تكون إلا في الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects the claim that swimming must be in water, noting that a horse stretching its forelegs while running is also called a swimmer.
rows.anchor: قلنا ؛ لا نسلم فإنه يقال في الفرس الذي يمد يديه في الجري سابح

rows.speaker: جمهور الفلاسفة وأصحاب الهيئة
rows.claim: Most philosophers and astronomers describe the spheres as solid bodies, neither heavy nor light, incapable of rupture, joining, growth, or decay.
rows.anchor: وقال جمهور الفلاسفة وأصحاب الهيئة : إنها أجرام صلبة لا ثقيلة ولا خفيفة غير قابلة للخرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the spheres' qualities cannot be known except through transmitted reports.
rows.anchor: والحق أنه لا سبيل إلى معرفة صفات السموات إلا بالخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi lays out three possibilities: a stationary sphere with moving stars; moving spheres and stars, in the same or opposite directions and at varying or equal speeds; or moving spheres with stationary stars fixed in them.
rows.anchor: فإنه إما أن يكون الفلك ساكنا والكواكب تتحرك فيه كحركة السمك في الماء الراكد ، وإما أن يكون الفلك متحركا

rows.speaker: جمهور الفلاسفة وأصحاب الهيئة
rows.claim: Philosophers reject the first two possibilities because they would rupture the spheres, and settle on stars fixed in moving spheres.
rows.anchor: فلم يبق إلا القسم الثالث وهو أن يكون الكوكب مغروزا في الفلك واقفا فيه والفلك يتحرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects the premise that spheres cannot rupture, says all three arrangements are possible for God, and takes the Qur'an's apparent wording to favor fixed spheres with stars swimming through them like fish in water.
rows.anchor: بل الحق أن الأقسام الثلاثة ممكنة والله تعالى قادر على كل الممكنات والذي يدل عليه لفظ القرآن

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the tanwin on kull substitutes for an annexed noun, meaning all of them swim in an orbit.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : { كل } التنوين فيه عوض عن المضاف إليه

rows.speaker: أبو علي بن سينا
rows.claim: Avicenna argues that the planets are living and rational because the masculine rational plural form is used and because Joseph saw the sun, moon, and stars prostrating.
rows.anchor: احتج أبو علي بن سينا على كون الكواكب أحياء ناطقة بقوله : { يسبحون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi replies that the rational plural is used because the stars are described by an action, swimming; it does not prove that they are rational beings.
rows.anchor: والجواب : إنما جعل واو الضمير للعقلاء للوصف بفعلهم وهو السباحة

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the clause is either an accusative circumstantial clause attached to sun and moon or an independent resumption with no syntactic slot.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : فإن قلت الجملة ما محلها قلت النصب على الحال من الشمس والقمر أو لا محل لها لاستئنافها

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Asked how all can swim in one orbit when each has a separate orbit, al-Zamakhshari compares it to saying the prince clothed them in one robe: each received its own.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت : لكل واحد من القمرين فلك على حدة فكيف قيل جميعهم يسبحون في فلك ؟

rows.speaker: رضوان بن عبد المعبود
rows.claim: The phrase was read nukkisū with gemination, or nukkisū in the passive, meaning they turned themselves upside down; the passive reading is attributed to Ridwan ibn Abd al-Ma'bud.
rows.anchor: وهي قراءة رضوان بن عبد المعبود

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains af as a sound whose utterance signals that the speaker is annoyed.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : أف صوت إذا صوت به علم أن صاحبه متضجر

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Abraham was exasperated by their persistence in worship after their excuse failed and truth became clear, so he voiced his displeasure.
rows.anchor: وإن إبراهيم عليه السلام أضجره ما رأى من ثباتهم على عبادتها بعد انقطاع عذرهم ، وبعد وضوح الحق وزهوق الباطل

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: One possibility is that Abraham spoke after they had already recognized that his argument was sound.
rows.anchor: ثم يحتمل أنه قال لهم ذلك وقد عرفوا صحة قوله

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Another possibility is that the proof had become apparent although they had not understood it.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أنه قال لهم ذلك وقد ظهرت الحجة وإن لم يعقلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi favors the second timing: the proof was evident but they had not grasped it, as suggested by Abraham's questions about worship and reasoning.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الأقرب لقوله :
